title: Migrating Between TypeScript Versions knowledge check

questions.prompt: What should a production-oriented TypeScript project demonstrate?
options: Explicit contracts, runtime validation, tests for failures, secure configuration and reproducible delivery steps.
Type annotations as a replacement for authorization and validation.
A working happy path without tests or documentation.
Secrets committed into client bundles for convenience.
questions.answer_key: Explicit contracts, runtime validation, tests for failures, secure configuration and reproducible delivery steps.
questions.explanation: Production readiness requires runtime, security, testing and operational evidence beyond type checking.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Migrating Between TypeScript Versions”?
options: The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with reading release notes and checked against its intended contract.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with reading release notes and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Reading release notes”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Migrating Between TypeScript Versions”?
options: Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check compiler and dependency compatibility, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume updating configuration and resolving errors is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
questions.answer_key: Check compiler and dependency compatibility, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Compiler and dependency compatibility”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
